title: A seasonal NAO adjustment lowered winter rainfall trends in England and Wales in 1951-2025
abstract: We tested whether a linear North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) adjustment removes winter rainfall trends in two country averages. We used 75 winters from Met Office HadUK-Grid rainfall and NOAA CPC monthly NAO. The raw trends were 7.02 mm per decade in England and 16.14 in Wales. Adjustment for mean winter NAO lowered them to 5.27 and 6.35 mm per decade. Conditional 95% five-winter residual block intervals were -0.63 to 11.07 and -4.03 to 16.75. These intervals include zero but do not show that the trends are absent. England had a positive interval with separate monthly NAO terms and with ten-winter blocks. Wales remained uncertain in all planned checks. The result shows model-dependent evidence for a trend after this simple circulation adjustment. It does not separate all circulation effects or establish a climate cause. The package includes monthly inputs, source hashes, code, resampling draws, results and an independent numerical check.

display.caption: Winter rainfall and raw and adjusted trends. The intervals use paired five-winter residual blocks. Solid curves show centered 11-winter means after subtraction of the fitted NAO term. This adjustment does not remove all circulation effects.

citations.reason: Earlier campaign work tested forecast gain in the same country rainfall series. We ask a different question about trends, with new code and the same raw snapshots.
Weather-pattern adjustment and climate model experiments provide a broader framework. Our single-index test cannot reproduce that attribution.
Prior work warns about early-record precipitation biases. We limit the analysis to 1951 onward.
